title: Service Trust Weave: cross-functional SLO implementation plan
content:
Summary:
This doc is a working implementation plan for the "Service Trust Weave" program — a cross-functional effort to establish a lightweight, repeatable SLO lifecycle (definition -> telemetry -> error budget policy -> runbooks -> rollouts) for customer-visible model-serving surfaces and platform control plane APIs. Aim is to get three pilot services to steady-state SLOs and onboard 4 feature teams by end of Q3 2026.

Why "weave"?
- Weave = interleaving engineering, product, SRE, and CS obligations so dependability is owned end-to-end rather than layered.
- Focus on minimal viable guardrails that enable safe launches and fast rollbacks.

High-level objectives (measurable):
- Define clear SLOs for 3 pilot services (hosted-api-generation, embeddings-batch, model-routing) by 2026-07-15.
- Instrument per-route telemetry with target 99.9% collection fidelity for latency and error signals by 2026-07-29.
- Establish error budget policy, escalation ladder and automated rollback hooks for pilots by 2026-08-12.
- Run two simulated incidents (game days) and validate on-call playbooks with feature teams by 2026-08-30.
- Onboard 4 feature teams to the lightweight SLO template and cadence by 2026-09-30.

Scope (in) and (out):
- In: model-serving API endpoints (generation/chat/embeddings), control-plane route decisions, per-customer latency windows for hosted and dedicated tiers.
- Out: long-term platform redesigns (separate program), deep kernel/runtime optimizations (serving-runtime team), full enterprise audit retention (separate compliance engagement).

Primary stakeholders and roles:
- Program lead: Aisha Kapoor (platform-engineering) — coordinates cross-team delivery, prioritization.
- SRE coach: Diego Morales (site-reliability-engineering) — SLO design, oncall playbooks, ops runbooks.
- Product partner: Rina Patel (product-hosted-api) — defines customer intent, key journeys and severity mapping.
- CS liaison: Liam O'Neill (customer-success) — customer impact, comms and prioritization for enterprise accounts.
- Feature leads: (Priya Suresh, Maya Chen, Tom Alvarez, Farah Ibrahim) — own per-service implementation work.

Milestones and timeline (tentative):
- Week 1 (now -> 2026-06-21): kickoff, SLO taxonomy workshop, pick pilots.
- Week 2 (2026-06-22 -> 2026-06-28): measurement plan doc, list of telemetry gaps, lightweight sampling plan.
- Week 3-4 (2026-06-29 -> 2026-07-12): instrument metrics, create SLI collection dashboards, draft SLO objectives.
- Milestone A (2026-07-15): SLOs agreed and ratified by stakeholders.
- Week 6 (2026-07-16 -> 2026-07-29): automation for error budget calculation; cheap alerting (Slack + PagerDuty) stubs.
- Milestone B (2026-08-12): Error budget policy + rollback hooks wired into rollout pipeline (canary -> failover).
- Week 12 (by 2026-08-30): Game-day runs + postmortems.
- September: team onboarding, template adoption, exec readout.

Deliverables (per pilot):
- SLO spec (one-pager): owner, user journeys, SLI definitions, measurement method, target, burn-rate thresholds.
- Telemetry checklist: metrics, traces, sampling, retention needed for SLI compute.
- Error budget policy: thresholds, automated actions, escalation ladder, customer comms.
- Runbook (playbook): detection -> triage -> mitigation -> rollback -> postmortem template.
- Lightweight dashboard: per-route SLO status, burn rate, recent incidents, link to oncall.

Implementation notes and pragmatic constraints:
- Start with 90/95/99th latency windows for synchronous endpoints. Use p50/p95/p99 for internal monitoring but only p95/p99 for SLOs initially to keep signal-to-noise manageable.
- Use existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> Cortex -> Mimir) and add a daily job to compute SLO burn two ways (streaming and batch) to validate parity.
- Prefer incremental automation: begin with charting + manual calculation for first 2 weeks, then commit to cron-driven rollup, then add alerting.

Risks and mitigations:
- Telemetry gaps (risk): teams lack required spans/labels. Mitigation: measurement plan doc + two-day instrumentation sprint per pilot.
- Ownership ambiguity (risk): who paged for what? Mitigation: explicit escalation ladder in every runbook and stakeholder sign-off.
- False positives/alert fatigue: start with low-sensitivity alerts and refine via postmortems.

Communication plan:
- Weekly sync (30m) with program core (Aisha, Diego, Rina, Liam, feature leads) — Tuesdays 10:00 PT.
- Biweekly stakeholder demo for execs and product leadership (slides + 15m QA).
- Slack channel: #ops-weave (use for async updates and burn-rate alerts during pilot).
- Confluence landing page for artifacts: linked in metadata.

Runbook sketch (short):
- Detection: alert fires on burn-rate > 1.5x for 15m OR SLI breach sustained 5m.
- Triage: SRE lead checks dashboard, identifies candidate cause (model change? infra? routing?).
- Mitigation: if burn due to latency, shift traffic to lower-latency model variant or increase replicas; if errors, failover to compatible model variant with auto-backoff.
- Rollback: automated rollback via rollout pipeline if canary error rate > threshold for 3 successive 1m windows.
- Postmortem: templates + timeline + action owners in Confluence.

Experimentation and measurement plan (what to validate):
- Validate that burn rate calculation matches manual logs for 7 consecutive days.
- Simulate partial region outage and verify automatic fallback keeps customer-impacting SLOs within agreed limit.
- Measure mean time to detect and mean time to mitigate for pilot services; target MTTR reduction of 30% vs baseline.

Dependencies and blockers:
- Metrics retention increase (requires infra quota change) — PLAT-REQ-129 (blocking for telemetry).
- PagerDuty escalation mapping update — ops-admin ticket.
- Small changes to rollout service to support automated canary rollback hooks — see PR linked in metadata.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- SLO granularity: route-level vs surface-level for multi-tenant customers? Preliminary recommendation: start surface-level with per-customer tags for high-value customers.
- Burn window length: 28d or 7d rolling? Recommend 28d for stability, provide 7d short window for fast detection.
- Which business metrics map to user-visible severity levels? Rina to propose mapping by 2026-06-25.

Next actions (immediate):
- Aisha: schedule kickoff + invite core stakeholders (done).
- Diego: prepare SLO taxonomy slide and runbook template before 2026-06-18.
- Priya: confirm pilot services and Owners list by 2026-06-17.
- Rina: draft customer-impact severity mapping and add to Confluence page.
- Platform infra: open PLAT-REQ-129 and add to backlog (owner: platform-infra).

Notes to self / rough scratch:
- Keep templates tiny. We want adoption, not bureaucracy. One pager SLO + one paragraph runbook is enough for many services.
- Aim for reproducible onboarding: script that copies template, fills service name, creates dashboard and stub runbook.
- Keep CS informed of error budget policy so external comms are predictable.

Appendix: useful links and snippets
- Slack: #ops-weave, #sre-oncall
- Jira: PLAT-8423 (dashboard work), SRE-311 (runbook templates)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/586 (canary rollback hooks)
- Confluence landing: https://confluence.redwood.local/display/PLAT/Service+Trust+Weave+Landing+Page

Unresolved: need exact thresholds for canary rollback (proposal: 0.5% absolute error increase OR 2x baseline latency for 3 windows).

If you are reading and want to tinker: add notes directly in page below — this is intended to be a living plan.

--- end of working draft (comments welcome)
